title: LYNX LP Range Manager
protocolOverview: Lynxify runs LYNX, a yield aggregator on Hedera. Users deposit HBAR into an ERC-4626 vault, and a strategy manager invests it in SaucerSwap V3 liquidity positions and HBAR staking. This review covers the code added since the previous yAudit review: the paged LP harvest and the LP Range Manager. `SaucerSwapLiquidityStrategy` holds the vault's concentrated-liquidity positions. Its harvest now runs one page of collects or swaps per call, so each transaction stays under Hedera's limit of 50 child records. `LynxLpAllocator` gives each LP target a range policy. When a position stays out of range for a set number of weekly cycles, the allocator closes it and mints a new one around the pool's TWAP, and the owner and governance can widen or unwind a position in an emergency. `LynxKeeperRouter` runs the weekly loop through the Hedera Schedule Service in six phases, one per transaction: paged harvest, staking harvest, buffer refill and drain, range operations, surplus allocation and idle LP deployment. `LpRangeMath` and `TickMath` hold the range and price math. The live mainnet stack still runs the earlier four-phase keeper, and neither the paged harvest nor the LP Range Manager is deployed.
auditScope: This review covers 7 Solidity files, totaling approximately 3078 lines of code. It focuses on the changes since commit `ca33ab4`, the baseline after the previous yAudit review. It was an AI-driven review: AI agents searched the code, and the auditors triaged and verified every reported issue before including it in this report. The auditors also manually reviewed the most critical parts of the code. Some findings come from the yAudit Fellows' review of the same commit.

issues.title: One persistently reverting target starves range management of every later target
issues.body:
#### Technical Details

[`LynxKeeperRouter._rangeOps()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxKeeperRouter.sol#L695-L727) always walks the allocator targets from index zero and calls `rebalanceOne()` until one attempt is "used". The fix for [internal audit finding #7](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/docs/audits/lp-range-manager-deep-audit-2026-09.md) sets `rotated = true` in the `catch` branch as well as on success:

```solidity
if (!rotated) {
    try lpAllocator.rebalanceOne(t.positionSN, deadline) returns (bool r) {
        if (r) rotated = true;
    } catch {
        rotated = true; // at most one attempt per phase
    }
}
```

Bounding the phase to one attempt is needed to stay under Hedera's child-record cap. But every revert counts as the consumed attempt, and there is no persistent cursor between cycles. A target that reverts every week therefore keeps every target after it from ever reaching `rebalanceOne()`. [`_evaluateRotate()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxLpAllocator.sol#L1265-L1347) only runs inside `rebalanceOne()`, so for the skipped targets `oorStreak` never increments, the "in range" reset never runs, and no rotate can fire. The `checkRangeStatus()` call the router makes for them does not maintain this state. Monitoring does not see the condition either: after a reverted attempt `rotated` is `true`, so the phase emits [`RangeOpsCompleted(true, …)`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxKeeperRouter.sol#L733) as if a rotate had executed.

`rebalanceOne()` can revert persistently for several reasons:

- **Swap size versus pool depth.** The decrease of an out-of-range position returns a single leg, so the rotate needs the ratio swap. [`_swapSurplus()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxLpAllocator.sol#L724-L750) sells roughly half of the position's value, plus any idle balances the rotate sweeps in by design ([internal #15](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/docs/audits/lp-range-manager-deep-audit-2026-09.md)). Its `minOut` is a linear TWAP quote minus `swapSlippageBps` (default 1%), with no allowance for the pool fee or price impact. The strategy also caps execution at a TWAP-derived price limit (`harvestSwapSlippageBps`, 100 bps on sqrt, about 2% on price). When the swap is large relative to the pool's in-range depth, it cannot meet these bounds, and the rotate reverts on every attempt. On a 1% fee tier with the default slippage it fails in practice (see #12).
- **Spot displaced from the TWAP.** A position goes out of range because the price moved, and the rotate sells the leg the move pushed the position into. While the move continues, spot sits past the 30-minute TWAP in that direction. The swap falls short of its TWAP-based `minOut` once that displacement exceeds the margin left after the pool fee. Once spot is about 2% past the TWAP, the strategy's price limit is behind spot and the pool rejects the swap (`SPL`). `SpotTwapDeviationExceeded` and the NPM check on the TWAP-priced mint minimums fail in the same conditions.
- **An attacker-induced revert.** `_swapSurplus()` sizes the ratio swap from the strategy's _full_ WHBAR and pair-token balances. Anyone can donate pair tokens to the strategy and enlarge the swap until its own price impact breaks `minOut`. Every rotate attempt for that target then reverts. The same donation pattern blocks `drainPosition()` (see #5).
- **A short oracle buffer.** After the target-enabled and policy checks, and before any `_evaluateRotate()` gate, [`rebalanceOne()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxLpAllocator.sol#L530-L539) reads the TWAP tick through `_getTwapTick()`. That call reverts `TwapNotReady` when `observe([twapWindowSec, 0])` fails, while the `_isTwapReady()` check before it only compares `observationCardinality` with `minObservationCardinality` (default 2). A target with a range policy on a pool whose ring buffer does not cover the 1800 s window therefore reverts even when its position is in range. The same root cause is described for valuation in #15. It does not affect the current mainnet catalog: on 2026-10-08 the five catalog pools reported an observation cardinality of 500 to 1200, and all of them served `observe([1800, 0])`. It applies to newly added or low-cardinality pools.
- `InvalidRange` from `planRotate()` near the tick bounds, and `InsufficientMintFee` while the router treasury cannot fund the allocator.

Each revert rolls back the allocator's tracking writes but not the router's consumed attempt, so the same target reverts again the next week.

This is a regression from the fix for [internal finding #7](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/docs/audits/lp-range-manager-deep-audit-2026-09.md). Before that fix, a revert let the loop try the next target.

#### Impact

Medium. One target whose rotate keeps reverting can permanently disable automated range management for every target after it in `targets[]`. No attacker is needed: a position that is large for its pool's depth, or a 1% fee tier, is enough. An attacker can also force the condition by sacrificing pair tokens. The skipped positions can stay out of range indefinitely and earn no fees. Because `checkRangeStatus()` keeps reporting them as out of range, `oorDivertActive` stays set and phase 4 sends 100% of the vault surplus to staking every week, so the LP sleeve receives no new capital. The phase reports each reverted attempt as a rotate, so the pattern is easy to miss. Recovery requires an operator to notice it and then reorder or disable targets, freeze range ops, or use the emergency paths. No principal is transferred to an attacker.

#### Recommendation

Keep the one-execution-attempt budget, but stop a single target from consuming it forever:

- Advance a persistent selection cursor after every execution attempt, including failures, so a failing target cannot starve the others.
- Separate evaluation from execution. Run `_evaluateRotate()` for every enabled target, since it only reads the TWAP and writes streak state, then execute at most one confirmed candidate.
- Make the pre-gates non-reverting. In `rebalanceOne()`, use `LpRangeMath.tryTwapTick()` and `return false` (emitting `RotateSkipped("twap not ready")`) instead of reverting through `_getTwapTick()`. Make `_isTwapReady()` verify that `observe(twapWindowSec)` succeeds, not only the cardinality.
- Make the rotate swap executable. Include the pool fee in `minOut` (see #12), and size the swap from the balances the decrease produced rather than the strategy-wide balances, so a donation cannot inflate it. Because the replacement mint deploys the full balances by design ([internal #15](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/docs/audits/lp-range-manager-deep-audit-2026-09.md)), the mint amounts must follow the same scoping.
- Report a reverted attempt separately from an executed rotate. For example, emit an event in the `catch` branch with `positionSN` and the revert data, and add a distinct flag to `RangeOpsCompleted`.

#### Developer Response

Fixed in commits [25d3de3](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/25d3de3f4dbf75218144616d5ad06d53dc732fea), [7d3902b](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/7d3902b023ca9ad2d3222415695d99ac4f22c7a2), [f0384d3](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/f0384d35cc56eb5685b204b09c80766a58f377c4), [6cec9e0](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/6cec9e019fe9e75f49864e040f614e18d36c1b71).

issues.title: Permissionless `retrySchedule()` on phase 0 mid-pass postpones the cycle by a week and keeps the harvest lock
issues.body:
#### Technical Details

After the fix for [internal finding #6](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/docs/audits/lp-range-manager-deep-audit-2026-09.md), [`retrySchedule()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxKeeperRouter.sol#L329-L333) picks the delay from `opsPhase` alone:

```solidity
_scheduleNext(opsPhase == 0 ? weeklyIntervalSec : phaseGapSec);
```

The assumption is that `opsPhase == 0` always means "the 5→0 wrap just failed to schedule". With paged harvest, phase 0 has a second meaning: the router stays on phase 0 between harvest pages, and after a catchable phase-0 body failure, until the liveness caps trip ([L351-L355](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxKeeperRouter.sol#L351-L355)):

```solidity
if (from == 0 && _shouldStayOnPhase0(bodyOk)) {
    if (loopActive) {
        _scheduleNext(phaseGapSec);   // may emit ScheduleFailed and leave pendingSchedule == 0
    }
    return;
}
```

If this intra-cycle `_scheduleNext()` fails (HSS capacity, treasury, transient error), `pendingSchedule == 0` and the page or failure state is preserved. `opsPhase` alone cannot tell this continuation apart from a completed-cycle wrap. The next `retrySchedule()`, which anyone can call, including an ordinary recovery bot, schedules the next page `weeklyIntervalSec` (604,800 s) later instead of `phaseGapSec` (60 s). Once that schedule exists, further retries revert `PendingScheduleExists` and cannot bring execution forward. The keeper playbook even prescribes this retry: its recovery steps state that with `loopActive && pendingSchedule == 0` anyone can call `retrySchedule()` to run the current phase soon (`docs/keeper-playbook.md`, "Hedera 328").

For that week:

- When a pass is pending, `harvestPassActive` stays `true` on the LP strategy, so every path guarded by `_requireNoHarvestPass()` reverts: `createLPPosition()`, `closeLPPosition()`, `rotateClosePosition()`, `swapToWhbar()` and `swapFromWhbar()`. This blocks the governance/owner break-glass paths `emergencyUnwind()` and `emergencyWiden()`, as well as drain swaps and manual swaps. If the router stayed on phase 0 only because the first page of a pass failed, no lock is held and only the delay below applies.
- The rest of the current cycle is delayed by a full week: staking harvest, phase 2 `refillBuffer()` (the redeem buffer is not refilled from staking while withdrawals drain vault idle), range ops, surplus push and LP deploy.

#### Impact

Low. No funds are at risk, but a one-off HSS failure combined with a routine retry freezes LP emergency operations and buffer refill for a week. The router owner can recover through manual `weeklyOps()` calls or `stopWeeklyLoop()` + `startWeeklyLoop()`.

#### Recommendation

Remember the delay intended by the failed `_scheduleNext()` call and reuse it in `retrySchedule()`. Alternatively, treat phase 0 as a continuation whenever the cycle is mid-flight:

```diff
-        _scheduleNext(opsPhase == 0 ? weeklyIntervalSec : phaseGapSec);
+        bool midPhase0 = opsPhase == 0
+            && (ILpHarvestPaged(lpStrategy).harvestPassPending()
+                || lpHarvestPagesThisCycle != 0
+                || consecutivePhase0Failures != 0);
+        _scheduleNext(opsPhase == 0 && !midPhase0 ? weeklyIntervalSec : phaseGapSec);
```

#### Developer Response

Fixed in commit [1a35e8b](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/1a35e8b75749bf3ab1041e2b203162f3eddd8bc0).

issues.title: `emergencyWiden()` still depends on a ready TWAP close to spot, so it fails in the conditions it is advertised for
issues.body:
#### Technical Details

[`emergencyWiden()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxLpAllocator.sol#L546-L562) is documented as the break-glass path that "must always work", for "violent market moves, unready TWAP, or frozen automated range ops", with "No TWAP, no swap, no rotate gates" (NatSpec at [L546-L549](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxLpAllocator.sol#L546-L549)). It deliberately centres on the raw `slot0()` price so it can proceed when the regular spot-deviation guard would fail ([L637-L650](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxLpAllocator.sol#L637-L650)).

However, whenever the requested range contains spot, which is the normal goal of a widen, [`_swapWidenSurplus()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxLpAllocator.sol#L709-L720) runs the ratio swap. An old out-of-range position yields a single-token balance. The widen also invests the strategy's whole WHBAR balance, so the WHBAR leg may not be empty, but the two legs are almost never in the new range's ratio, so in practice re-ranging around spot almost always needs a non-zero swap. The swap was added by the fix for [internal finding #12](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/docs/audits/lp-range-manager-deep-audit-2026-09.md), and the NatSpec still describes the earlier swap-free path. Contrary to the NatSpec, the code therefore performs a swap, and that swap is TWAP-gated twice:

1. In the allocator, `LpRangeMath.quoteSurplusSwap()` → `SlippageQuotes.minOutFromTrustedPool()` → `trustedSqrtPriceX96()` reverts with `TwapNotReady` when cardinality is insufficient. It also reverts on any `observe()` failure, and with `SpotTwapDeviationExceeded` when spot deviates from the TWAP by more than `maxSpotDeviationBps` (default 500 bps on sqrt, about 10% on price).
2. In the strategy, [`_swap()` → `_deriveSwapPriceLimit()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/SaucerSwapLiquidityStrategy.sol#L1128-L1147) repeats `trustedSqrtPriceX96()` with the strategy's own TWAP configuration whenever no explicit `swapSqrtPriceLimitX96` override is set. Relaxing only the allocator's settings is therefore not enough.

The strategy's price limit is also the tighter bound. `_deriveSwapPriceLimit()` places `sqrtPriceLimitX96` at the strategy TWAP ± `harvestSwapSlippageBps` (default 100 bps on sqrt, about 2% on price). Re-ranging an out-of-range position around spot sells the leg the market moved the position into, so the swap trades in the direction of the move, and after a fast move spot is already past the TWAP in that direction. Once spot is about 2% past the TWAP, the limit is behind spot and the pool rejects the swap (`SPL`). Closer to the limit, the swap fills only up to it and fails `minOut`. In a violent move, the widen therefore reverts long before the 500 bps deviation bound is reached.

Any of these reverts rolls back the whole widen, including the preceding `rotateClosePosition()`. The allocator exposes no caller-selected emergency slippage bounds. The owner's only workaround is to relax `maxSpotDeviationBps` through the allocator's `setTwapConfig()`. Neither the strategy's TWAP configuration nor its `setSwapSqrtPriceLimitX96()` override, which would bypass the derived limit, has a passthrough on the allocator, so the second check and the limit cannot be relaxed without a strategy ownership handover. When the widen does not need a swap, these checks are skipped and it works as documented.

#### Impact

Low. The emergency re-range is unavailable in exactly the market and oracle conditions it was built for, contrary to its NatSpec. After a violent move, it only becomes executable once the 30-minute TWAP is within about 2% of spot. `emergencyUnwind()` does no swap and remains available while the harvest lock is clear, so funds can still be exited, just not re-ranged.

#### Recommendation

Give the emergency path explicit, caller-provided bounds, such as `swapMinOut` and `sqrtPriceLimitX96` or a `skipSwap` flag, and enforce them through both the allocator and a dedicated owner-only strategy swap entry that does not derive a TWAP limit. Do not weaken the regular rotate path. If oracle-independent widening is intentionally unsupported, document the restriction and direct emergency callers to `emergencyUnwind()` when the TWAP is unavailable or too far from spot.

#### Developer Response

Fixed in commits [8ca49b5](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/8ca49b5a44f5bb9634abe15f575527076927e404), [66eb6dd](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/66eb6dd8f14f276b476e5e4abd6a7c5edbee2841).

issues.title: The allocator's governance powers cannot be exercised through `LynxGovernor`
issues.body:
#### Technical Details

`LynxLpAllocator` gives its `governance` address (the DAO timelock) several powers:

- `setEnabledFlags()` (`onlyGovernance`), the DAO's control over which targets receive capital (`docs/governance-dao-mapping.md`), and therefore its trigger for the phase-2 drain of a deselected position. The owner can set the same flags through [`setTargets()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxLpAllocator.sol#L947-L955), which writes each target's `enabled` field.
- `setOpsRangeFrozen(false)`, described as "the DAO escape hatch so the owner cannot permanently disable range operations" ([L819-L837](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxLpAllocator.sol#L819-L837)).
- `emergencyWiden()` and `emergencyUnwind()`, owner OR governance.

With the Governor as its only proposer, the timelock only executes what [`LynxGovernor._propose()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/governance/LynxGovernor.sol#L143-L177) accepts. That function rejects any action with a non-zero `value` and only allows, on the allocator, the `setEnabledFlags()` selector, and only when the target equals the Governor's `immutable lpAllocator`:

```solidity
if (target == lpAllocator) {
    return selector == SET_ENABLED_FLAGS_SELECTOR;
}
```

This has two consequences:

1. **The emergency and unfreeze powers are unreachable by the DAO.** Proposals for `emergencyWiden()`, `emergencyUnwind()` or `setOpsRangeFrozen(false)` revert `ProposalActionNotAllowed`. The "DAO escape hatch" described in the NatSpec and playbook does not exist in the deployed governance stack. Even if these selectors were allowlisted, the governance latency would make them unsuitable for emergencies. On mainnet it is a 1-day voting delay, a 7-day voting period and a timelock delay of at least 48 hours. In the meantime a rotate can replace the targeted serial ([internal #18](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/docs/audits/lp-range-manager-deep-audit-2026-09.md)).
2. **After the Layer C rollout, the DAO cannot even call `setEnabledFlags()`.** The Governor pins `lpAllocator` as `immutable`, and on mainnet it returns the live allocator `0x…a52d05`. The rollout deploys a new allocator, because `lpStrategy` is immutable, and does not redeploy governance (one-pager, "Rollout for B (and B+C)"). Every proposal targeting the new allocator is therefore rejected. The DAO loses its only allocator power, while the owner keeps full control of target selection through `setTargets()`.

Even where the DAO could act, its role is not independent:

- [`setGovernance()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxLpAllocator.sol#L388-L392) is `onlyOwner` and takes effect immediately.
- The owner can override any DAO toggle at any time with `setTargets()`, and can disable automation through `setRangeRotateEnabled(false)`, which governance cannot reverse.
- The threat model assigns the timelock's `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` and the protocol `owner` to the same admin multisig (`docs/governance-threat-model.md`). On mainnet, the live allocator's `owner()` (`0xb19907cD…04bD`) holds `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` on the timelock. [`LynxTimelock._execute()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/governance/LynxTimelock.sol#L39-L47) only blocks role changes executed through the timelock itself. The admin can therefore grant itself `PROPOSER_ROLE` directly and schedule any call, including the emergency ops with a non-zero value. The `governance` branches are reachable by the admin, not by token holders.

#### Impact

Low. No funds are at risk, but the DAO controls advertised for the range manager are not available through governance. The unfreeze escape hatch and the emergency ops never were, and after the rollout target enable/disable is not either. All of them remain with the owner, who as timelock admin can also act through the `governance` address. The separation of powers that the NatSpec and playbook describe therefore does not exist in the deployed stack.

#### Recommendation

Before the Layer C rollout, deploy a Governor whose allowlist points at the new allocator, or make the allocator address in the Governor updatable through governance itself. Decide which allocator powers the DAO should hold and add them to the allowlist, at least `setOpsRangeFrozen` and, if intended, `emergencyUnwind`/`emergencyWiden`. If the DAO is not meant to hold them, remove the `governance` branches and correct the NatSpec and playbook. Consider letting only the current `governance` change `governance`. If the DAO is meant to constrain the owner, give the timelock's `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` to a different party than the protocol owner, or renounce it once the roles are final.

#### Developer Response

Fixed in commits [511a01b](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/511a01bb30b41cad0242d70c94afeb75221db180), [2354f6d](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/2354f6d2fcc571de0c7ac87db0feff471a1d6d06). The allocator is now owner-only, and the governor no longer allows any allocator selector.

issues.title: A pair-token donation can permanently block the drain of a disabled LP position
issues.body:
#### Technical Details

[`drainPosition()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxLpAllocator.sol#L1062-L1071) removes all liquidity from a disabled position. It then swaps the strategy's entire balance of the pair token to WHBAR through [`_swapPairBalanceToWhbar()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxLpAllocator.sol#L1143-L1154). The `minOut` comes from [`_minOut()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxLpAllocator.sol#L783-L798): a linear TWAP quote minus `swapSlippageBps` (default 1%), which ignores the pool fee and price impact. The strategy also caps execution at a TWAP-derived price limit (`harvestSwapSlippageBps`, 100 bps on sqrt). A sale large enough to move the pool past that margin fills short of `minOut` and reverts.

Anyone can transfer the pair token to the strategy. A donation sized to push the sale past the margin makes every drain of that position revert. The donation is not undone by the reverted drain, and nothing else converts it: the harvest swap page only sells credited fees, and the allocator has no generic swap path (see #14). [`reconcileInactiveLp()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxKeeperRouter.sol#L398-L427) retries the first disabled position above dust every week, without a `try/catch`. That position is therefore never drained, and the disabled positions after it in `lpPositionSerials` are never reached. Each failure also rolls back the phase-2 buffer refill (see #6).

The same revert occurs without a donation when the position is large relative to the pool's in-range depth. It also occurs on a 1% fee tier with the default slippage (see #12).

The full-balance sweep was reported in the previous engagement (yAudit/linxify-report#6) for its imprecise scope. The client kept the sweep by design and documented it. That issue did not cover this denial of service. The same donation pattern in the rotate swap is part of #1.

#### Impact

Low. By sacrificing pair tokens, an attacker can keep a governance-disabled position, and every disabled position after it, out of the automated drain indefinitely. Through #6, the same failure also suppresses the weekly buffer refill. The donation becomes protocol value, and the position remains recoverable through `emergencyUnwind()` and a strategy ownership round trip, so no funds are lost.

#### Recommendation

Swap only the pair balance that the decrease produced. `drainPosition()` already records `pairBalBefore`, so the position-scoped amount is the balance after the decrease minus `pairBalBefore`. Sweep pre-existing balances through a separate owner-gated, size-bounded swap, which would also give the unwound residual in #14 a conversion path. If the full sweep must stay by design, cap the amount swept beyond the position's own proceeds so that a donation cannot make the sale unexecutable, and include the pool fee in `minOut` (see #12).

#### Developer Response

Fixed in commits [239aa3d](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/239aa3d01089b3d7c73f1abef3cd72eddd85e920), [8197b10](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/8197b102395506b69402fa78dc124f0df9331c81).

issues.title: A failed drain rolls back the same phase's buffer refill
Drain proceeds are not pulled back once the LP strategy's principal reaches zero
issues.body:
#### Technical Details

[`_pullLpRecoveredWhbar()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxKeeperRouter.sol#L580-L589) pulls the LP strategy's idle WHBAR back to the vault after a drain, but returns early when the strategy has no recorded principal:

```solidity
if (manager.principalOf(lpStrategy) == 0) return;
```

The manager tracks one aggregate principal for all LP positions, and every pull reduces it by the WHBAR received, capped at the remaining basis. A profitable wind-down, in which earlier drains return more than their share of basis, can therefore bring principal to zero while other positions are still open. From then on, the value of those positions is unrealized gain, which cost-basis accounting keeps out of NAV until a pull realizes it.

The guard blocks that realization. When governance later disables and drains another position, its proceeds stay on the strategy instead of returning to the vault, and phase 5 may redeploy them into the remaining enabled targets. The guard is not needed for accounting. With zero basis, [`StrategyManager.pull()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/StrategyManager.sol#L215-L243) reduces no principal, and [`_bookPullRealization()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/StrategyManager.sol#L270-L277) reports the whole receipt as gain, which then streams into NAV through profit locking.

This was filed during the previous fix review (yAudit/linxify-report#36) and closed without changes. The code is unchanged in this delta.

#### Impact

Low. Realized LP value stays outside NAV and redemption liquidity until new principal is pushed to the strategy and a later drain triggers a pull that recovers it. Shares minted in the meantime are priced against understated assets and share in the eventual recovery. Reaching zero principal with positions still open requires a profitable wind-down, so the likelihood is low.

#### Recommendation

Remove the zero-principal guard so that every successful drain returns its proceeds to the vault. `StrategyManager.pull()` already books receipts above the remaining basis as gain.

#### Developer Response

Fixed in commit [6377792](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/6377792ecfc8e771915ad3dde7126d2d094f35a6).

issues.title: Owner-side harvest-lock hatches on the LP strategy are unreachable once the allocator owns it
issues.body:
#### Technical Details

The LP strategy documents two ways to clear a stuck harvest pass:

- [`resetHarvestPass()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/SaucerSwapLiquidityStrategy.sol#L463-L467), `onlyOwner`, described as "the emergency hatch" in the contract NatSpec.
- [`abortHarvestPass()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/SaucerSwapLiquidityStrategy.sol#L472-L477), owner or `StrategyManager.keeper()`.

In production the strategy's owner is `LynxLpAllocator`. The allocator never calls either function and has no generic passthrough, so the owner branch is dead code. The only live caller is the keeper router, and only from `_advanceOpsPhase(0)` and `stopWeeklyLoop()`, the latter only while `loopActive`.

One reachable state is left without a direct hatch. [`startWeeklyLoopAndRun()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxKeeperRouter.sol#L282-L297) runs a phase-0 page that leaves `harvestPassActive == true`, then fails to schedule. It returns with `loopActive == false`, so `stopWeeklyLoop()` reverts `LoopNotActive`. `lpHarvestPagesThisCycle` is also left non-zero and is inherited by the next `startWeeklyLoop()`. Until the router owner drives the pass to completion by calling `weeklyOps()` by hand, or restarts the loop, every `_requireNoHarvestPass()` path is blocked, including `emergencyUnwind()` and `emergencyWiden()`.

#### Impact

Informational. Recovery is possible through the router owner, or by pointing `StrategyManager.keeper()` at an EOA. The advertised strategy-level hatch, however, cannot be used, and the emergency paths depend on keeper liveness.

#### Recommendation

Add an owner-only `resetHarvestPass()` passthrough on the allocator. In `startWeeklyLoopAndRun()`, when scheduling fails, abort any pending pass and reset `lpHarvestPagesThisCycle` / `consecutivePhase0Failures`, the same way `stopWeeklyLoop()` does.

#### Developer Response

Fixed in commits [f58eb85](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/f58eb8585a455a140c4761dd840e55d7df6f7499), [cff5d62](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/cff5d62eb24eeb6b4e0c38cf7a1f76bb5b1c744e).

issues.title: OOR divert flag is computed from pre-rotate state, so a successful rotate can still divert the week's surplus
issues.body:
#### Technical Details

In [`_rangeOps()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxKeeperRouter.sol#L707-L731), `checkRangeStatus(t.positionSN)` is evaluated and folded into `anyOor` *before* `rebalanceOne()` is called for the same target. If that target was out of its raw range and is the one that rotates, its new position is centred on the TWAP and in range. `anyOor` still holds the stale `true`, though, and `_setOorDivertActive(anyOor)` arms the divert. Phase 4 then sends 100% of the cycle's surplus to staking, even though no target is out of range anymore. This does not happen on every rotate: `rebalanceOne()` can also fire while the TWAP is only inside the `oorBufferTicks` wing, where `checkRangeStatus()` still reports the position as in range.

#### Impact

Informational. The LP sleeve can miss one week of new capital after a rotate, which skews the target split toward staking.

#### Recommendation

Re-evaluate the rotated target after a successful `rebalanceOne()`, by calling `checkRangeStatus(newSN)` through `getActivePositionSN(i)`. Alternatively, compute `anyOor` in a second pass after the rotate attempt.

#### Developer Response

Fixed in commit [fd32346](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/fd32346c8dab04f473e933535e7cf1b99dce6750).

issues.title: `emergencyWiden()` is not payable and depends on the allocator's leftover HBAR for the mint fee
issues.body:
#### Technical Details

[`emergencyWiden()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxLpAllocator.sol#L575-L673) forwards `lpStrategy.mintFeeHbar()` as `{value: w.mintFee}` to `createLPPosition()` from the allocator's own balance, but the function itself is not `payable`. The router only tops the allocator up to one mint fee during phase 3 (`_fundAllocatorMintFeeIfNeeded()`), and a keeper rotate in the same cycle consumes it. A widen executed afterwards fails with a bare low-level revert from the value transfer. Unlike the rotate path, it has no `InsufficientMintFee` pre-check, and the caller cannot attach HBAR to the call. This is the `emergencyWiden()` residual of [internal finding #17](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/docs/audits/lp-range-manager-deep-audit-2026-09.md), whose fix (PT-026) funds the allocator only for the keeper's rotate.

#### Impact

Informational. The break-glass call can fail for an operational reason that is unrelated to the market and gives no clear error.

#### Recommendation

Operationally, the caller can pre-fund the allocator in a separate transaction, since `receive()` is open to anyone. A DAO batch cannot do this: `LynxGovernor` rejects proposals with a non-zero `value` and does not allow `emergencyWiden()` (see #4). In code, make `emergencyWiden()` `payable` (and refund any excess), or add the same `InsufficientMintFee` pre-check as `_finishRotate()` and document that the allocator must be pre-funded before an emergency widen.

#### Developer Response

Fixed in commit [12719c9](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/12719c9e2fde41ed2e5effd923e9099d93cfc9cf).

issues.title: A partially filled harvest swap erases the fee credit of tokens that were not sold
issues.body:
#### Technical Details

[`_swapHarvestPage()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/SaucerSwapLiquidityStrategy.sol#L902-L928) caps the requested swap input at `harvestFeeCredit[pairToken]`. After a successful call it subtracts the entire *requested* input from the credit, without measuring how many pair tokens actually left the strategy:

```solidity
harvestFeeCredit[pairToken] -= balance;
_clampHarvestFeeCredit(pairToken);
```

The requested input is not guaranteed to be fully spent. [`_swap()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/SaucerSwapLiquidityStrategy.sol#L1106-L1147) passes a non-zero `sqrtPriceLimitX96`, either configured or derived from the TWAP minus `harvestSwapSlippageBps`. A SaucerSwap V2 pool stops at that limit even if input remains, and the router accepts the result whenever `amountOutMinimum` is met. Payment follows the pool's actual input delta (see the [pool](https://github.com/saucerswaplabs/saucerswaplabs-v2-core/blob/master/contracts/UniswapV3Pool.sol#L609) and [router](https://github.com/saucerswaplabs/saucerswaplabs-v2-periphery/blob/master/contracts/SwapRouter.sol#L104-L118) implementations). The price limit and the output minimum are distinct protections, so a near-complete partial fill can satisfy `minOut`. For example, spot may already sit close to the TWAP-derived limit when the page executes. The strategy has no full-consumption check.

When only part of the credited amount is sold, the credit still drops to zero while unsold fee tokens remain. `_clampHarvestFeeCredit()` can only lower credit, never restore it, and the swap cursor advances.

From then on:

- The residual has no credit, so later harvests never swap it as fees. It is only converted when a strategy-wide sweep absorbs it: `_swapSurplus()` and the replacement mint in a rotate or `emergencyWiden()`, or `drainPosition()`.
- `_tryIdlePairTokenWhbarValue()` no longer subtracts a credit for it, so it is valued as ordinary idle principal.

The residual is small. `minOut` is `slot0` value × (1 − `harvestSwapSlippageBps`) on the *whole* requested amount, while the output of the filled part is at most its spot value × (1 − pool fee). The sold fraction must therefore be at least (1 − s) / (1 − fee). With the default s = 1%, at most about 0.7% of the page's credited fees can remain unsold on a 0.3% pool. On a 1% pool a partial fill can essentially never pass `minOut` (see #12).

#### Impact

Informational. A small fraction of a page's fees, bounded by about `harvestSwapSlippageBps` minus the pool fee, can leave automated fee realization until a later rotate, widen or drain sweeps it. When the strategy is impaired, that residual raises settled NAV through impairment release instead of passing through `reportGain()` and profit locking. The funds stay in the strategy.

#### Recommendation

Measure the pair-token balance before and after `_executeHarvestSwap()`, debit the credit only by the input actually spent, and keep the unsold credited remainder available for a later page. Report the actual input in `HarvestPairSwapped`, and apply `_clampHarvestFeeCredit()` after the measured debit.

#### Developer Response

Fixed in commits [acbb297](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/acbb297688655e227da226d4585f67ad0388d4be), [2354f6d](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/2354f6d2fcc571de0c7ac87db0feff471a1d6d06).

issues.title: Swap `minOut` quotes ignore the pool fee, so swaps on 1% pools fail in practice
issues.body:
#### Technical Details

[`_quoteMinWhbarOut()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/SaucerSwapLiquidityStrategy.sol#L967-L977) prices the input at the pool's `slot0()` spot price, without the pool fee, and applies only `harvestSwapSlippageBps` (default 100 = 1%):

```solidity
uint256 quoted = _tokenWhbarValue(pairToken, pool, amountIn); // spot value, no fee
minOut = quoted * uint256(10_000 - bps) / 10_000;
```

The swap output is at most `quoted × (1 − poolFee)`, before any price impact. On a 1% pool (`poolFee = 10000`), the best possible output equals `minOut`, so the swap fails whenever price impact exceeds the margin left by rounding. With the default configuration, `_executeHarvestSwap()` therefore reverts on practically every non-trivial page. The revert is caught (`HarvestPairSwapFailed`) and counts against `maxHarvestSwaps`. On a 0.3% pool, only 0.7% is left for price impact. The catalog `hardhat/config/lp-pools.json` contains a 1% WHBAR/DOVU pool (currently `selected: false`).

The allocator's quotes have the same omission. [`SlippageQuotes.minOutFromTrustedPool()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/libraries/SlippageQuotes.sol#L167-L181) applies only `swapSlippageBps` (default 100) to `quoteExactInput()`, which is documented as "no fee haircut". It prices the `deployLpIdle()` swap and the drain swap through [`_minOut()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxLpAllocator.sol#L783-L798). In the delta, it also prices the rotate and widen ratio swap through `LpRangeMath.quoteSurplusSwap()`. With a 1% target enabled and the default `swapSlippageBps`, these swaps fail in practice for the same reason:

- `deployLpIdle()` reverts at that target's swap whenever `swapBps > 0` (the catalog uses 5000). The [deploy loop](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxLpAllocator.sol#L1044-L1054) has no per-target isolation, so the phase-5 deploy fails for every target, not only the 1% one. Any other per-target revert, such as a transient spot/TWAP deviation on one pool, has the same effect for that week. The undeployed WHBAR stays on the strategy. As long as phase 4 keeps pushing surplus (it does not during a divert), the idle balance grows for every target until the next rotate sweeps it into a single position ([internal #15](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/docs/audits/lp-range-manager-deep-audit-2026-09.md)), which also enlarges that rotate's swap (see #1).
- Every confirmed rotate of that target reverts. This is one of the persistent reverts that starve later targets in #1.
- A drain of that target reverts as well, so a deselected 1% position stays in the pool and the phase-2 buffer refill is rolled back with it (see #5 and #6).

#### Impact

Informational. With the default slippage settings, enabling a 1% pool has three effects. First, harvest does not convert its pair-token fees in practice: they stay credited and excluded from NAV, never stream as profit, and every page spends a swap attempt, and its child records, on a swap that cannot succeed. Second, the weekly LP deploy fails for all targets, so the LP sleeve's new capital stays idle. Third, the pool's own position can neither rotate nor be drained. The owner can restore the allocator paths by raising `swapSlippageBps` (up to 500 bps, for every pool at once). `harvestSwapSlippageBps` can only be changed through a strategy ownership handover, since the allocator has no passthrough for `setHarvestSwapConfig()`.

#### Recommendation

Include the pool fee in both quotes, `_quoteMinWhbarOut()` and `SlippageQuotes.minOutFromTrustedPool()`, for example `minOut = quoted × (1 − poolFee) × (1 − slippageBps)`. Alternatively, require the slippage settings to exceed the fee of every tracked pool. Switching the harvest quote to the TWAP price alone does not fix the omitted fee. Deploy each target in isolation, for example through a per-target self-call wrapped in `try/catch`, so that one failing target keeps its share for the next cycle instead of blocking the others.

#### Developer Response

Fixed in commits [50cc7fc](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/50cc7fcb57dd095f3c37332a260095b6d090347d), [a7194b1](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/a7194b17dbcbb41b547095aa1ed90129eac4a68e), [1e4fb25](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/1e4fb251119fd50fd6dcb4f3cd3e8a9f0adfe63f).

issues.title: Settlement valuation relies on a raw pool TWAP and counts unsolicited pair-token balances
issues.body:
#### Technical Details

`impairmentValue()` is used by `StrategyManager.syncValuations()` before every vault deposit, mint, withdraw and redeem. It values the LP strategy's positions and the full directly held balance of every tracked pair token, minus `harvestFeeCredit`, at the pool's 30-minute TWAP. This happens in [`_tryIdlePairTokenWhbarValue()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/SaucerSwapLiquidityStrategy.sol#L782-L827) and `_tryTotalLpWhbarValue()`. Two design properties follow:

1. The valuation does not distinguish strategy-generated balances from donations. Anyone can transfer a tracked pair token to the strategy, and it is valued immediately.
2. The TWAP is read through `tryTwapSqrtPriceX96()` without a spot-deviation bound or any independent oracle. Omitting the spot/TWAP veto is intentional: it is the fix for a previous finding (M-06 of the earlier engagement, "Spot deviation can veto impairment synchronization").

The settlement price is therefore only as robust as the 30-minute TWAP of each configured pool. A shareholder who could keep a shallow pool's TWAP pushed up would inflate the valuation, release reversible impairment at the next sync, and redeem against the restored accounted principal. When the TWAP normalizes, the remaining shareholders absorb the difference. A donation alone is not an accounting error: the donor gives up real value, and the impairment it releases is legitimate. It only amplifies such a manipulation by the difference between the manipulated and the real price.

We have not demonstrated that this manipulation is profitable for any pool in the catalog. That depends on the cost of moving the TWAP, the exploitable impairment, the attacker's share and the redeemable liquidity. We therefore report it as a design observation. It differs from M-01 of the previous engagement, which covered *unvalued* pair balances causing false loss booking, the opposite case.

#### Impact

Informational. Settlement safety depends on the depth and observation history of every configured pool. The upside is bounded by the strategy's outstanding impairment and reduced by the exit fee.

#### Recommendation

Restrict the catalog to pools whose TWAP is costly to move over `twapWindowSec`, and size `twapWindowSec` and cardinality accordingly. Consider valuing idle pair tokens as at most `min(actualBalance, recognizedBalance)`, where `recognizedBalance` only changes through verified strategy operations, and capping how much impairment a single sync may release.

#### Developer Response

Fixed in commits [ea82bc7](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/ea82bc7cc2227ca3a6c6972abbc363bfaef346d2), [cb7af3b](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/cb7af3b19cf5bebc0d8788028adf45b153be7458), [14e04d9](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/14e04d970940fd72c1608999e351e358328c9c29), [4472608](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/447260836e4a38059da5a651c850a7c2d632e6ad), [44c58e7](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/44c58e72e4c4cba83ae0c6965a32fd593f30d52d).

issues.title: The post-unwind recovery in the NatSpec and keeper playbook omits the required strategy ownership handover
issues.body:
#### Technical Details

[`emergencyUnwind()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxLpAllocator.sol#L1083-L1123) burns the NFT through `closeLPPosition()`, sets `targets[idx].positionSN = 0`, and leaves both legs idle on the strategy. That the target then needs a new NFT is known and documented. [Internal finding #16](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/docs/audits/lp-range-manager-deep-audit-2026-09.md) accepts that it stays enabled. The playbook ("Recovery path after unwind", `docs/keeper-playbook.md`) and `taskplane-tasks/CONTEXT.md` ("Bootstrapping flow") describe re-entry as: the owner "mints a fresh LP position on `SaucerSwapLiquidityStrategy`" and re-points the target with `setTargets()`.

The allocator cannot perform that step. The strategy's `createLPPosition()` is `onlyOwner`, and the strategy's owner is the allocator, which exposes no `createLPPosition()` passthrough. `deployLpIdle()` skips `positionSN == 0` ([L1052](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxLpAllocator.sol#L1052)) and only calls `increaseLPPosition()`. `rebalanceOne()` and `emergencyWiden()` both need a live serial, and `setTargets()` → `_validateTarget()` requires an existing active NFT. The `emergencyUnwind()` NatSpec, which says "re-entry requires a fresh `setRangePolicy()` + `deployLpIdle()`" ([L1079](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxLpAllocator.sol#L1079)), is also inaccurate.

The allocator cannot convert the non-WHBAR leg left by the unwind either:

- `drainPosition()` needs a non-zero serial (`_resolvePairToken()` reverts `PositionNotFound(0)`), and the burned serial is no longer in `lpPositionSerials`, so `reconcileInactiveLp()` never reaches it.
- The harvest swap page caps each swap at `harvestFeeCredit`, which only grows from fee-only collects, so the unwound principal is never sold.
- Rotates of other targets only swap their own `pairToken`.
- The allocator has no generic `swapToWhbar()` passthrough.

Both the re-entry and the residual conversion therefore require an Ownable2Step round trip of the LP strategy: `transferLpStrategyOwnership()` to the operator, manual operations, transfer back, then `acceptLpStrategyOwnership()`. The repository already supports this round trip as a general recovery procedure (`ops:mainnet:lp-reclaim-strategy` and `ops:mainnet:lp-return-strategy`). The keeper playbook documents it for a configuration change that was applied on mainnet on 30 Aug 2026. The unwind documentation does not refer to it. During the round trip the allocator is not the owner, so every keeper path that reaches an `onlyOwner` strategy function through the allocator (`deployLpIdle()`, `drainPosition()`, `rebalanceOne()`) reverts. The playbook asks for the loop to stay stopped until ownership is back.

#### Impact

Informational. No funds are lost. The residual stays valued in `impairmentValue()` through the tracked pair, and the existing reclaim and return scripts make both re-entry and residual conversion possible. The unwind NatSpec and the playbook's recovery section, however, describe a re-entry the allocator cannot perform. They also omit the ownership round trip, which pauses automated LP operations while it lasts.

#### Recommendation

At minimum, correct the NatSpec on `emergencyUnwind()` / `ILynxLpAllocator.emergencyUnwind()` and point the playbook's "Recovery path after unwind" to the reclaim/return procedure. To avoid the round trip, add an owner-only re-entry function that mints a new position for a target with `positionSN == 0`, reusing `_swapSurplus()` + `_mintPlanned()` with caller ticks (the same as `emergencyWiden()` minus the close). Add an owner-gated, TWAP-protected `swapPairResidualToWhbar(pairToken, amountIn, minOut)` passthrough as well.

#### Developer Response

Fixed in commits [bd9e39c](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/bd9e39ce8236eb61c9158b4ef0a42fb833059b37), [5b4f45a](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/5b4f45a635b6a73652f9f3bb76a6daec37b34d23), [81d1d8a](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/81d1d8a8981fdadd286a5da980db2c231ac308fa).

issues.title: Cardinality is treated as TWAP readiness, so a pool with short observation history can block vault settlement
issues.body:
#### Technical Details

`TwapQuotes.tryTwapSqrtPriceX96()` only checks `observationCardinality >= minObservationCardinality` (default 2) before calling `observe([twapWindowSec, 0])` with a 1800 s window. Cardinality does not prove that the ring buffer actually covers the window. SaucerSwap V2 pools overwrite the oldest observation once capacity is reached, and `observe()` reverts (`OLD`) if the oldest retained sample is younger than the requested window. Nothing on-chain enforces more than `minObservationCardinality = 2`, and the only provisioning script in the repository (`hardhat/testing/warm-saucerswap-twap.ts`, testnet-only) grows pools to exactly 2. At cardinality 2, two observations written within 30 minutes are enough. The oracle writes at most one observation per block timestamp, on tick-changing swaps and in-range liquidity changes.

In [`SaucerSwapLiquidityStrategy`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/SaucerSwapLiquidityStrategy.sol#L750-L827), both `_tryTotalLpWhbarValue(true)` and `_tryIdlePairTokenWhbarValue(true)` return `(false, 0)` when any relevant pool fails. This covers every active position with non-zero liquidity (`_tryTotalLpWhbarValue()` skips the TWAP read when `pos.liquidity == 0`, [L758](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/SaucerSwapLiquidityStrategy.sol#L758)). It also covers every tracked pair token with a configured pool and a non-zero balance net of `harvestFeeCredit`, including the idle pair token left behind by a drained position. The dust exemption only applies to pair tokens without a pool ([L809-L813](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/SaucerSwapLiquidityStrategy.sol#L809-L813)). `impairmentValue()` then reports an incomplete valuation, and `StrategyManager.syncValuations()` reverts `ImpairmentValuationFailed`. Every vault deposit, mint, withdraw and redeem runs this sync, so all of them revert while the condition lasts.

`tryTwapSqrtPriceX96()` already catches the `observe()` failure and fails closed, so the code behaves as designed. The problem is that nothing provisions or checks enough observation history. With a small buffer, ordinary pool activity can trigger the outage, and an attacker can sustain it with small tick-changing swaps. In the delta, the same assumption also drives `checkRangeStatus()` (permanent OOR divert) and the `rebalanceOne()` revert described in #1.

The current mainnet catalog is not in this state. On 2026-10-08 the five pools in `hardhat/config/lp-pools.json` reported the following observation cardinalities: 1200 for USDC, DOVU and SAUCE, 1000 growing to 1200 for HBARX, and 500 for PACK. All of them served `observe([1800, 0])`. The shortest buffer, PACK's, reached back about 9.6 days. Exhausting any of them within 30 minutes would take 500 to 1200 writes at distinct block timestamps in every window, for as long as the attacker wants the outage to last. The assumption is still neither enforced nor checked. A pool whose buffer was never grown stays at cardinality 1 and fails `twapPriceReady()` outright, which is why the testnet pools needed the warm-up script. A pool grown only to 2 fails under ordinary trading.

#### Impact

Informational. With the current catalog, normal activity cannot cause the outage, and forcing it would take a sustained, costly stream of swaps. If a pool with a small observation buffer is added, vault deposits and redemptions, including redemptions from the idle buffer, are suspended while it cannot serve the 30-minute observation. No funds are extracted, and anyone can fix it permanently by calling `increaseObservationCardinalityNext()` on the pool. The fix is not immediate: the new slots only fill as observations are written, and the ring buffer must then cover the 30-minute window.

#### Recommendation

Raise the observation cardinality of every valuation-relevant pool well above the number of observations writable within `twapWindowSec`, and set `minObservationCardinality` on the strategy and allocator to that level. Before funding a position or registering a pool, check that `observe([twapWindowSec, 0])` succeeds, and use that same check, rather than cardinality alone, in `twapPriceReady()` / `_isTwapReady()`. Keep valuation fail-closed and do not fall back to spot.

#### Developer Response

Fixed in commits [644d444](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/644d444e7da2d664f14e806a3796bb7fab7e7c09), [fa530e6](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/fa530e675a576456da104d111b63b5bd11f9e4d5), [9788149](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/97881497f43d8823d7238fdc70513824793b1547).

issues.title: The playbook's stop/start recovery replays phase 3 and can confirm a rotate on a single out-of-range observation
issues.body:
#### Technical Details

`RangePolicy.minOorCycles` is the number of "consecutive weekly phases OOR before rotate fires" (default 2, [`ILynxLpAllocator`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/interfaces/ILynxLpAllocator.sol#L33)). [`_evaluateRotate()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxLpAllocator.sol#L1265-L1347) enforces it by counting calls: every call that finds the TWAP outside the band increments `oorStreak`, and nothing checks how much time has passed since the previous increment. The weekly spacing therefore depends on phase 3 running once per cycle.

The documented recovery breaks that assumption:

- After a consumed 328 abort, the playbook prescribes `stopWeeklyLoop()` followed by `startWeeklyLoop()` (`docs/keeper-playbook.md`, "Hedera 328", step 2).
- The ledger lists phases 4 and 5 as able to 328 on their own (`docs/audits/keeper-lp-review-2026.md`).
- [`stopWeeklyLoop()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxKeeperRouter.sol#L305-L320) resets `opsPhase` to 0, and [`startWeeklyLoop()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxKeeperRouter.sol#L267-L274) schedules phase 0 one `phaseGapSec` later.

Phases 0 to 3 therefore replay within minutes of the phase 3 that already ran in that cycle. The same happens when the loop is stopped for a strategy ownership round trip and restarted within the same cycle.

On the replayed phase 3, every target that is still out of range gets a second streak increment from a 30-minute TWAP window that overlaps the first one almost entirely. With the default `minOorCycles = 2`, a target whose first out-of-range observation came minutes earlier reaches the threshold. Gate 6b compares two almost identical ticks and only resets the streak if the TWAP moved back in between, so an unchanged or further TWAP confirms the rotate.

The internal audit described this consequence for a premature `retrySchedule()` ([internal finding #6](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/docs/audits/lp-range-manager-deep-audit-2026-09.md): "the streak is counted twice on overlapping TWAP windows, so a premature rotate is possible"). Its fix only changed the delay `retrySchedule()` uses, so the prescribed stop/start path still replays phase 3 within the same cycle.

#### Impact

Low. A rotate can be confirmed from a single out-of-range observation when the loop is restarted after phase 3. That happens when operators follow the documented recovery after a 328 in phase 4 or 5, or restart the loop after an ownership round trip. In that case `minOorCycles` no longer protects against rotating on a transient move, so the rotate crystallizes impermanent loss and swap costs.

##### PoC (if any)

Scenario, not executed:

1. Target A has `minOorCycles = 2` and no recent rotate. In week N its TWAP leaves the band, and phase 3 records `oorStreak[A] = 1`.
2. Phase 5 of week N aborts with 328, which leaves a stale `pendingSchedule`.
3. Following the playbook, the operator runs `stopWeeklyLoop()` and `startWeeklyLoop()`. Phases 0 to 3 replay a few minutes later.
4. Phase 3 evaluates A again. The streak reaches 2, and Gate 6b sees `currDist >= prevDist` because the TWAP has barely moved, so the rotate executes in week N.

#### Recommendation

Make the confirmation time-based. Record when a target's streak last counted an out-of-range observation, and ignore observations closer than about one `weeklyIntervalSec` to it. Alternatively, record when `_rangeOps()` last ran and skip the rotate attempt when a restart replays phase 3 within the same interval.

#### Developer Response

Fixed in commit [93a62a2](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/93a62a2b2c6205e864789a4f30be38b3171fc2bd), together with #20.

issues.title: `deployLpIdle()` swaps a fixed share of each target's budget regardless of its range, so concentrated and out-of-range targets leave much of every deploy idle
issues.body:
#### Technical Details

For every enabled target, [`_swapAndPrepareAmounts()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxLpAllocator.sol#L1580-L1607) swaps `perTarget × swapBps / 10_000` WHBAR into the pair token. `swapBps` is a single global value (5000 in the catalog). [`_increaseLpPosition()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxLpAllocator.sol#L1557-L1578) then adds both legs. The NPM only takes as much of each leg as the position's current ratio requires, and the rest stays on the strategy.

A fixed split fits the full-range positions the allocator was built for, whose value split stays close to 50/50. Layer C makes targets concentrated, and the ratio of a concentrated position depends on where the price sits inside its range. It is 50/50 only at the geometric centre and reaches 100/0 at the edges. A rotate only re-centres a target after `minOorCycles` weekly confirmations, so positions spend most of their life off-centre. For example, if the position is 80/20 by value at the current price, a 50/50 deposit is limited by the scarce leg, and 37.5% of the budget stays idle.

An out-of-range target accepts only one token. Phase 5 still swaps half of that target's budget, adds the accepted leg single-sided to a position that earns no fees, and leaves the other leg idle. When the accepted leg is the pair token, the deploy keeps buying the token the market moved against and parks it in an inactive range. That is the opposite of what the OOR divert is meant to do ("keeps new capital out of an LP position that cannot earn"). The playbook notes that phase 5 "still runs after a divert" (`docs/keeper-playbook.md`).

What stays idle is not wasted outright, but it is not productive either:

- Idle WHBAR is re-split in later weeks and goes through the same 50/50 swap again.
- Idle pair tokens are not credited fees, so harvest does not convert them. They wait for the next rotate's full-balance sweep ([internal #15](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/docs/audits/lp-range-manager-deep-audit-2026-09.md)).
- Every unused swap also pays the pool fee and price impact.

`LpRangeMath.quoteSurplus()` already computes the correct ratio for a given range and price, but only the rotate and widen paths use it.

#### Impact

Low. With concentrated ranges, a large and recurring share of the LP sleeve's weekly capital does not reach the liquidity it was pushed for, and out-of-range targets keep receiving single-sided adds. Yield is lost and swap costs are paid for nothing, but no principal is lost.

#### Recommendation

Size each target's deploy swap with `LpRangeMath.quoteSurplus()`, from the target's WHBAR budget and its range at the TWAP, as the rotate and widen paths already do. For targets whose TWAP is outside their range, either skip them and leave their share for the next cycle, or deploy only the leg they accept without swapping. With per-target sizing, `swapBps` is no longer needed.

#### Developer Response

Fixed in commit [48375e7](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/48375e7cc1598395d3760c21e6158ed3e1abf7eb).

issues.title: Rotates keep deploying idle capital while the vault is paused
issues.body:
#### Technical Details

The vault guardian can pause the vault in response to an incident. Since the fix for yAudit/linxify-report#19 in the previous engagement, the pause also halts deployment: while `vault.paused()` is true, `pushAndDeploy()`, `deployLpIdle()` and `allocateSurplus()` return early ([L434](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxKeeperRouter.sol#L434), [L445](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxKeeperRouter.sol#L445), [L536](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxKeeperRouter.sol#L536)), and `StrategyManager._precheckPush()` reverts. During a pause, WHBAR already pushed to the LP strategy therefore stays idle.

The rotate added in Layer C does not respect the pause:

- [`_rangeOps()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxKeeperRouter.sol#L664-L734) gates only on the allocator, `opsRangeFrozen` and the harvest lock.
- `rebalanceOne()` adds no pause check.

The replacement mint deploys the strategy's full WHBAR and pair-token balances ([internal #15](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/docs/audits/lp-range-manager-deep-audit-2026-09.md)). A rotate during a pause therefore does more than re-range the rotated position: it also invests the idle WHBAR that `deployLpIdle()` is holding back. Only the owner can stop this, through `setOpsRangeFrozen(true)`; the guardian cannot.

#### Impact

Informational. If an incident leads the guardian to pause the vault, the keeper can still move idle capital into a new LP position until the owner also freezes range ops. The rotate's TWAP and slippage checks still apply.

#### Recommendation

Skip `rebalanceOne()` in `_rangeOps()` while the vault is paused, keeping the divert computation, or let the guardian freeze range ops.

#### Developer Response

Fixed in commit [6dcd5b4](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/6dcd5b4cdb7015fd37731aba2ee8b0fdb9773cff).

issues.title: Phase 2 overflows the 50 child-record cap
issues.body:
#### Technical Details

The keeper runs the weekly cycle as one HIP-1215 scheduled transaction per phase so that each transaction stays under Hedera's 50 child-record cap. Phase 2 does not stay within that budget. [`_weeklyOpsBody()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxKeeperRouter.sol#L748-L754) runs [`refillBuffer()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxKeeperRouter.sol#L380-L395), [`reconcileInactiveLp()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxKeeperRouter.sol#L398-L427) and [`_pullLpRecoveredWhbar()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxKeeperRouter.sol#L580-L589) in one transaction, and [`weeklyOps()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxKeeperRouter.sol#L348-L361) appends `deleteSchedule` and `scheduleCall` to it.

`refillBuffer()` pulls from the composite staking strategy, which pays from its native leg first and then swaps its XSAUCE, DOVU and HBARX hold legs. Each hold-leg swap is sized with an exact-output quote that ignores the pool fee, so each leg returns slightly less than requested and the refill moves on to the next leg. Once the native leg is empty, a refill swaps all three legs. The drain adds a decrease, a collect and a full-balance swap, and the recovery pull adds a second `manager.pull()`.

The overflow needs two conditions in the same week:

1. The composite native leg is empty. Under sustained net redemptions this happens after roughly 10% of TVL in cumulative outflow, because pushes refill the native leg only on surplus.
2. A funded LP position is not an enabled target, so a drain is pending. This follows any owner removal or deselection with `setTargets()`. On mainnet, phase 2 has been draining four unselected funded positions (NFTs 76609 to 76612), one per week: 76609 on 29 September, 76610 on 6 October and 76611 on 13 October. 76612 is still funded and is next.

A Hardhat test running the production router, allocator, LP strategy, manager, vault and composite staking contracts traces 68 child records for phase 2 at one target, and 67 to 76 at 1, 4 and 8 targets. These are modelled counts: the mocks do not enforce the cap or emit status 328. The model counts each HTS call, including `balanceOf` reads, as one record. If HTS reads produced no records, phase 2 would be about 18 to 20 records and would fit. The client's own mainnet measurements ([keeper playbook](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/docs/keeper-playbook.md#L306-L307): a swap at 7 to 8 records with about 3 mutating calls, a collect at 4.4 with 2 transfers) indicate that reads do count.

Status 328 cannot be caught, so the whole transaction rolls back. `opsPhase` stays at 2 and `pendingSchedule` still names the consumed schedule, so `retrySchedule()` reverts. The documented recovery (stop, then start the loop) replays phases 0 to 2 into the same overflow while both conditions hold.

This is related to, but not covered by, these issues:

- Internal residual AD-4 does not list phase 2.
- #6 covers the same phase-2 coupling for catchable reverts.

#### Impact

Low. While both conditions hold, the weekly loop stops at phase 2. The buffer refill, the drain, the recovery pull and phases 3 to 5 do not run, and redemptions are limited to the vault's idle balance. No funds are lost and NAV is unchanged because the rollback is total.

The owner can restore the loop without code changes. After a stop and start, the owner calls `refillBuffer()` directly, which `onlyOpsExecutor` allows. That runs the three-leg swap in its own transaction. The next scheduled phase 2 then carries only the drain and the recovery pull, modelled at about 37 records, and commits. No attacker is required and no one profits.

#### Recommendation

Move `reconcileInactiveLp()` and `_pullLpRecoveredWhbar()` out of phase 2 into their own scheduled phase immediately after the refill, as #6 also suggests. In that phase:

- Attempt one `drainPosition()` per transaction.
- Run the recovery pull in the same revert scope as that drain.
- Advance a round-robin cursor so that one failing position does not block the others.

Do not rely on try/catch inside the current phase 2. A caught revert on Hedera still commits its child records, so the transaction can still exceed the cap.

Until the split ships, add phase 2 to the AD-4 residual list and to the 328 runbook, including the `refillBuffer()` recovery above. After the split, phase 2 alone is modelled at about 45 to 48 records with the native leg empty. Measure it on a Hedera testnet.

#### Developer Response

Fixed in commits [79d4d3d](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/79d4d3d21621fc81987352432f27777b6848a8ad), [619c5ee](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/619c5eeab47b4e4ad460eba2df021578b03cdaac).

issues.title: Stale oorStreak lets a target rotate early
issues.body:
#### Technical Details

`LynxLpAllocator` documents `oorStreak` as counting ["consecutive weekly OOR phases"](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxLpAllocator.sol#L136-L137) with a reset on reentry, and the default `minOorCycles = 2` exists so that a single out-of-range reading does not trigger a rotate. The streak has no time key. [`_evaluateRotate()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxLpAllocator.sol#L1265-L1347) increments it on every out-of-range evaluation and resets it only at [Gate 5](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxLpAllocator.sol#L1310-L1315), when it evaluates the target and finds it in range.

Range ops does not evaluate every enabled target each week:

- The router makes at most one `rebalanceOne()` attempt per run. A successful rotate, or a caught revert, of an earlier target sets `rotated = true`, so later targets are not passed to `rebalanceOne()` that week ([L715-L726](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxKeeperRouter.sol#L715-L726)). This one-attempt rule is the fix for internal finding #7. The loop still reads each target's `checkRangeStatus()`.
- A frozen range phase returns before the loop ([L676-L680](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxKeeperRouter.sol#L676-L680)).
- The TWAP-readiness pre-check ([L519-L535](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxLpAllocator.sol#L519-L535)) also skips Gate 5.

A target that comes back into range in a skipped week therefore keeps its old streak and `lastOorTick`:

1. Week N: concentrated targets A (index 0) and B (index 1) both read out of range. Each gets streak 1.
2. Week N+1: A rotates, or its rotate reverts and is caught. B is back in range but is not evaluated, so it keeps streak 1.
3. Week N+2: B leaves the band again, at least as far as in week N. B reaches streak 2 and rotates on this one new reading, although the previous week was in range.

The minimum-gap fix proposed in #16 does not close this path, because the stale reading is more than one interval old. The fix for internal finding #9 resets only the target that rotated.

A Hardhat test using the production router, allocator, LP strategy, StrategyManager and vault reproduces it. A's rotate in week N+1 leaves `oorStreak(B) = 1` while `checkRangeStatus(B)` reports in range, and B then rotates in week N+2 from `[-600,600]` to `[60,1320]`. In the control, B's in-range week is evaluated, its streak resets, and week N+2 produces only a candidate.

#### Impact

Low. The vault pays for one premature rotate of one LP position: the pool fee and up to `swapSlippageBps` on the swapped surplus, plus fees forgone if the price returns and the new range is out of range. Nothing is locked, and no third party gains beyond ordinary arbitrage. The outcome equals one rotate under the owner-permitted `minOorCycles = 1`.

It requires two or more concentrated targets that go out of range together, followed by an out, in, out price sequence. The current `lp-pools.json` targets are full-range.

#### Recommendation

1. On each unfrozen range-ops run, evaluate Gate 5 for every enabled, active target, independent of the single rotate attempt. At minimum, reset the streak when the target is in range. The router already reads `checkRangeStatus()` for each target.
2. Restart the streak at 1 when the previous out-of-range reading is older than about one `weeklyIntervalSec` plus slack, so a skipped or frozen week restarts confirmation instead of counting toward it.

For the same-week replay, see #16.

#### Developer Response

Fixed in commits [51e02c7](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/51e02c7438a9d34ff5de2426b86950c3e190f26f), [93a62a2](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/93a62a2b2c6205e864789a4f30be38b3171fc2bd), [25d3de3](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/25d3de3f4dbf75218144616d5ad06d53dc732fea), [e1ad890](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/e1ad8906cfcd356fe27dd1cd6d516645af35629d).

issues.title: Harvest swap backlog can outgrow one swap
issues.body:
#### Technical Details

[`_swapHarvestPage()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/SaucerSwapLiquidityStrategy.sol#L880-L936) sells each pair token's full `min(balance, harvestFeeCredit[pairToken])` in a single `exactInputSingle()` call ([L902-L906](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/SaucerSwapLiquidityStrategy.sol#L902-L906)), with no per-swap cap. Its minimum output, from [`_quoteMinWhbarOut()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/SaucerSwapLiquidityStrategy.sol#L967-L977), is linear in the amount, while the pool's actual output falls behind it as the size grows because of the pool fee and price impact.

When a swap fails, the catch branch only clamps the credit to the token balance ([L930-L934](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/SaucerSwapLiquidityStrategy.sol#L930-L934)). Each later collect adds to the credit ([`_creditHarvestFees()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/SaucerSwapLiquidityStrategy.sol#L1223-L1227)), so the credit only grows. Once it exceeds a pool-depth threshold, every later swap fails at the same pool state. At the default 100 bps that threshold is about 0.71% of the in-range pair reserve at fee 3000 and about 0.86% at fee 1500. The retained tokens stay excluded from NAV until they are swapped.

A Hardhat test using the production strategy, manager and vault, with a router built on SaucerSwap V2's `SwapMath.computeSwapStep`, reproduces it:

- Configuration: WHBAR/PACK, fee 3000, full range, and a chosen 150 PACK of fees per week.
- After two failed weeks, every swap from week 3 to week 10 fails at the original price, leaving 1,500 PACK (about 148.7 WHBAR) unconverted.
- A control run without the initial failures converts every week.

This differs from #12, where a fee-blind minimum output makes 1% tier swaps fail every week. Here the cause is the growing credit, and a pool-fee haircut alone does not remove it.

#### Impact

Informational. Nothing is lost. The pair-side fees of one target stay on the strategy, excluded from NAV and not streamed as profit, until in-range liquidity grows or the owner raises `harvestSwapSlippageBps`. As #12 notes, raising it requires a strategy ownership handover from the allocator. In testing, raising the tolerance to 200 bps cleared the full backlog on the next pass.

It is unlikely on the current setup. On the launch USDC/WHBAR target Lynx holds about 0.3% of the pool, and reaching the threshold would take roughly 600 to 700 consecutive failed weeks. It becomes realistic only if Lynx holds a large share (10% to 33% or more) of a thin fee-1500 or fee-3000 pool.

#### Recommendation

Add an owner-set, per-pair-token cap on each harvest swap, at least the dust threshold. Swap at most one capped chunk per token per pass, and leave the remaining credit for later passes. For the credit debit after a partial fill, apply the fix recommended in #11.

#### Developer Response

Fixed in commit [4e975c3](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/4e975c36e29384ef4f156f4d6fca8425d0a9ecea).

issues.title: `_onChainLiquidity()` reads the wrong word of the production `positions()` return, so rotates and both emergency exits always revert
issues.body:
#### Technical Details

[`_onChainLiquidity()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/SaucerSwapLiquidityStrategy.sol#L1161-L1176) reads a position's liquidity from the raw return data of the NPM's `positions()`:

```solidity
if (!ok || ret.length < 0x100) { /* bubble up */ }
assembly {
    liquidity := mload(add(ret, 0x100))
}
```

`mload(add(ret, 0x100))` loads return word 7, counting from 0. That is `liquidity` in the 12-word Uniswap V3 layout. The repository declares that layout in its [`ISaucerSwapV2NonfungiblePositionManager`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/SaucerSwapLiquidityStrategy.sol#L83-L96) interface and implements it in [`MockSaucerSwapV2NftManager.positions()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/mocks/MockSaucerSwapV2NftManager.sol#L194-L210).

The production SaucerSwap V2 NPM (`0.0.4053945`) returns 10 words, without `nonce` and `operator`. See `NonfungiblePositionManager.positions()` in its [verified source](https://hashscan.io/mainnet/contract/0.0.4053945/source):

```text
token0, token1, fee, tickLower, tickUpper, liquidity,
feeGrowthInside0LastX128, feeGrowthInside1LastX128, tokensOwed0, tokensOwed1
```

In production, `liquidity` is word 5 and word 7 is `feeGrowthInside1LastX128`. The length check still passes, because the return is 320 bytes. A read of the live launch position on 2026-10-12 shows the mismatch:

| `positions(76608)` | Value |
|---|---|
| Word 5 (`liquidity`) | 43,684,291,439. This equals the liquidity that mainnet strategy `0.0.10824909` stores for the serial. |
| Word 7 (`feeGrowthInside1LastX128`) | About 2.04 × 10³⁸ |

[`closeLPPosition()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/SaucerSwapLiquidityStrategy.sol#L656-L659) and [`rotateClosePosition()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/SaucerSwapLiquidityStrategy.sol#L699-L702) both decrease the returned amount before `burn`.
