The NPM rejects a decrease larger than the position's liquidity, so both functions revert. The only exception is a fee-growth word of zero, which effectively never occurs. Three allocator paths go through these functions:

- **Keeper rotate:** [`_finishRotate()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxLpAllocator.sol#L1463-L1474) first decreases the stored liquidity, then calls `rotateClosePosition()` to collect and burn. That decrease also refreshes the position's fee-growth snapshot, so word 7 is still non-zero.
- **[`emergencyWiden()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxLpAllocator.sol#L631)**, through `rotateClosePosition()`.
- **[`emergencyUnwind()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxLpAllocator.sol#L1112)**, through `closeLPPosition()`.

The repository tests use the 12-word mock, so they pass.

The read was added by the fix for [internal finding #3](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/docs/audits/lp-range-manager-deep-audit-2026-09.md) (PT-012), which protects the close paths against liquidity that a third party donates to the NFT:

- `ca33ab4` decreased the stored `position.liquidity`.
- PT-012 (`2810bb2`) decoded `positions()` through the 12-word interface. That decode would also have reverted on the 10-word return.
- `281eafb` replaced it with the raw word-7 read.

The mainnet strategy `0.0.10824909` predates this change. The issue applies from the deployment of the new strategy.

#### Impact

Medium. From the first day of the new strategy, the range manager cannot rotate any position, and both break-glass paths revert in every market condition.

- **Rotates:** the keeper's attempt reverts every week. Phase 3 catches the revert, counts it as the week's attempt and reports it as a rotate (see #1). The first confirmed target therefore also blocks every target after it.
- **Out-of-range positions:** they stay out of range and earn no fees, and the divert keeps sending the surplus to staking.
- **Emergency exits:** `emergencyWiden()` and `emergencyUnwind()`, the documented escape hatches, are unusable.

Principal is not lost. The drain path decreases the stored liquidity ([`_decreaseDisabledPosition()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxLpAllocator.sol#L1126-L1140)), so the owner can disable a target and let phase 2 drain it, subject to #5 and #12.

#### Recommendation

Read `liquidity` from word 5 and require the exact production return length:

```diff
-        if (!ok || ret.length < 0x100) {
+        if (!ok || ret.length != 0x140) {
             assembly {
                 revert(add(ret, 0x20), mload(ret))
             }
         }
         assembly {
-            liquidity := mload(add(ret, 0x100))
+            liquidity := mload(add(ret, 0xc0))
         }
```

Also align the interface and `MockSaucerSwapV2NftManager.positions()` with the 10-word production layout, and fix the NatSpec ("the 8th return"). Add a mainnet-fork test that checks `_onChainLiquidity()` against the stored liquidity of a live position.

#### Developer Response

Fixed in commit [b794fbf](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/b794fbfc8f73d5cb6cf58dc2e7cbef207519b585).

issues.title: LP minimums are priced at the TWAP while the NPM fills at spot, so rotates and deposits on concentrated ranges revert after a few ticks of drift
issues.body:
#### Technical Details

[`LpRangeMath.planDeploy()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/libraries/LpRangeMath.sol#L264-L280) sizes the liquidity and both minimums at the price it receives:

```solidity
uint128 liq = LiquidityAmounts.getLiquidityForAmounts(sqrtPriceX96, sqrtA, sqrtB, amount0Desired, amount1Desired);
(uint256 amount0, uint256 amount1) = LiquidityAmounts.getAmountsForLiquidity(sqrtPriceX96, sqrtA, sqrtB, liq);
return (_applyMinBps(amount0, lpSlippageBps), _applyMinBps(amount1, lpSlippageBps));
```

The allocator always passes the 30-minute TWAP:

- **Rotate mint:** [`_mintPlanned()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxLpAllocator.sol#L764-L779) uses the TWAP captured once per rotate ([L1413-L1416](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxLpAllocator.sol#L1413-L1416)).
- **Weekly deposit:** [`_increaseLpPosition()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxLpAllocator.sol#L1557-L1578) uses `_trustedSqrtPriceX96()`, which returns the TWAP once the spot-deviation check passes.
- **Drain of a disabled position:** [`decreaseMins()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxLpAllocator.sol#L1136-L1138) prices the minimums at the same TWAP.

The NPM sizes the liquidity at the pool's current `slot0()` price, then rejects the call if either amount used is below its minimum. On a full-range position, the token split barely moves with price. On a concentrated range it moves quickly, so a small gap between spot and the TWAP leaves one token short by more than `lpSlippageBps`. The default is 100 bps and the maximum is 500.

**Rotate mint.** The surplus swap targets the TWAP ratio, so the post-swap balances match the TWAP split and each minimum is about 99% of the balance. At any other spot price, one token is under-used, so the mint fails in both directions. The table gives the gap in ticks at which the mint fails, for a range centred on the TWAP, computed with Uniswap V3 liquidity math:

| Half-width | `lpSlippageBps` = 100 | `lpSlippageBps` = 500 |
|---|---|---|
| ±240 | 2 ticks | 7 ticks |
| ±600 | 3 ticks | 16 ticks |
| ±6000 | 27 ticks | 133 ticks |

**Other paths.**

- **Weekly deposit:** its desired amounts come from a fixed-share swap at spot (see #17), so it fails in one direction only.
- **Drain decrease:** a ±600 position centred on the TWAP fails at 6 ticks.
- **`emergencyWiden()`:** it prices its mint at spot, but it reads spot ([L642](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxLpAllocator.sol#L642)) before its own surplus swap ([L650](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxLpAllocator.sol#L650)). When the new range contains spot, the mint at [L654](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxLpAllocator.sol#L654) executes at the price the swap moved, so a concentrated widen can fail on the swap's own price impact, as the rotate does. A full-range widen, or one whose new range does not contain spot (no swap), is not affected.

A gap of a few ticks between spot and the 30-minute TWAP is the normal state of an active pool. On 2026-10-12 at 13:50 UTC, USDC/WHBAR spot was 4.4 ticks from its TWAP and SAUCE/WHBAR spot was 19.1 ticks away. At those gaps, a ±600 rotate would revert on USDC at the default setting, and on SAUCE even at the 500 bps maximum.

The current positions are full range and unaffected. #22 currently makes every rotate revert earlier, so this issue appears once #22 is fixed.

#### Impact

Medium. Concentrated ranges are what the range manager is for, and once they are in use:

- **Rotates** fail in most weeks. Each failed rotate consumes the week's attempt and blocks later targets (see #1). The out-of-range position earns nothing, and the divert keeps sending the surplus to staking.
- **Weekly deposits** often fail, and the target's WHBAR stays idle on the strategy.

No principal is lost.

#### Recommendation

Do not just move the minimums to spot. The TWAP-priced minimums also protect the mint against a manipulated spot price. Either:

- compute the minimums at spot, and bound the spot/TWAP gap for LP calls with a separate, tight limit (for example 50–100 bps). In the rotate and in `emergencyWiden()`, read spot after the surplus swap, not before it; or
- pass loose per-token minimums, and after `mint()` or `increaseLiquidity()` require the value received, at the TWAP, to be at least `1 - lpSlippageBps` of the value spent, also at the TWAP. Apply the same check to decreases.

#### Developer Response

Fixed in commits [ced1133](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/ced11335f592e5e1abf9f66a966a741c8db9270e), [3623754](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/362375444f96111b6132f4207d7c3a4259b2c655), [ecf1cff](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/ecf1cff1414b084db07540e3f33421840a49fc0b), [a2dcd18](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/a2dcd18e45c95f4a05247c1d341f99c9dd6d8287), [2354f6d](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/2354f6d2fcc571de0c7ac87db0feff471a1d6d06), [9ebaf30](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/9ebaf30838cda7b7a7dccd82fa1194fe720afd87).

issues.title: The fixed LP mint fee overpays SaucerSwap, and the excess is refunded to the next NPM caller
issues.body:
#### Technical Details

`mintFeeHbar` defaults to 1 HBAR ([L177](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/SaucerSwapLiquidityStrategy.sol#L177)). The strategy forwards it in full on every mint and increase: [`createLPPosition()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/SaucerSwapLiquidityStrategy.sol#L546-L549) and [`increaseLPPosition()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/SaucerSwapLiquidityStrategy.sol#L601-L604).

The production NPM does not consume the whole amount. In its [verified source](https://hashscan.io/mainnet/contract/0.0.4053945/source), `LiquidityManagement.addLiquidity()` reads the factory's `mintFee()`, which is set in tinycents. It converts the fee through the exchange-rate precompile, adds 1 tinybar for rounding, and forwards only that amount to the pool. The rest stays on the NPM. `PeripheryPayments.refundETH()` is permissionless and sends the NPM's entire HBAR balance to its caller. Neither strategy function calls it or checks its HBAR balance afterwards, so the excess goes to whoever calls `refundETH()` next.

Two mainnet transactions show this:

1. In `0xce638de3be8b624037478d7e7a1b6a1e181992ecb1e069b46107156586ba0d4e`, strategy `0.0.10824909` forwards 100,000,000 tinybar to the NPM. The NPM forwards 63,520,295 to the pool, so 36,479,705 tinybar stays on the NPM.
2. The next direct NPM call, `0x88ef00e540c9f0bbfe0dfb174aaa2af5456d9714908a0e2430fa131f609284fa`, comes from an unrelated account. Its own unused HBAR is 12,652,942 tinybar, but `refundETH()` pays it 49,132,647. The difference, 36,479,705, is exactly the strategy's leftover.

On 2026-10-12:

- the factory's `mintFee()` is 500,000,000 tinycents;
- the exchange rate is 30,000 HBAR = 278,664 cents;
- the NPM therefore charges 53,828,267 tinybar, and each mint or increase leaves about 46,171,733 tinybar (0.46 HBAR) for the next caller.

The code predates the delta. The delta adds paying call sites: the rotate and widen replacement mints ([`_mintReplacement()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxLpAllocator.sol#L1354-L1380)), funded by the allocator, in addition to the weekly per-target increases funded by the router.

The allocator has no passthrough for `setMintFeeHbar()`. Once it owns the strategy, the fee can only be changed through a strategy ownership handover.

#### Impact

Low. About 0.46 HBAR leaves the router or allocator treasury for an arbitrary third party on every LP mint and increase, which means every weekly deposit per target and every rotate or widen. The loss is direct and repeats every week, but it is small. A lower `mintFeeHbar` reduces it, but no fixed value removes it, because the required fee moves with the exchange rate.

#### Recommendation

Call the NPM's `refundETH()` in the same transaction, immediately after each `mint()` and `increaseLiquidity()`, or batch both through the NPM's `multicall()`. The strategy already has a `receive()` function, so it can receive the refund. Alternatively, compute the exact fee before each call from `factory.mintFee()` and the exchange-rate precompile, plus SaucerSwap's 1-tinybar rounding allowance.

#### Developer Response

Fixed in commits [fbe16f4](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/fbe16f4696baca006460eeecf871ebd8be74cc4e), [ecbf405](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/ecbf40598f3cf6bf6675a659ed929453aa75fb2a), [2354f6d](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/2354f6d2fcc571de0c7ac87db0feff471a1d6d06).

issues.title: A reverting collect blocks the paged harvest for every later position
issues.body:
#### Technical Details

[`_collectHarvestPage()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/SaucerSwapLiquidityStrategy.sol#L860-L872) walks `lpPositionSerials` from `harvestCollectIndex` and calls [`_collect()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/SaucerSwapLiquidityStrategy.sol#L1195-L1206) on each active serial. `_collect()` makes a single NPM `collect()` that transfers both tokens to the strategy. If either transfer fails, the whole page reverts, including the cursor increment. The swap page isolates failures per token (`HarvestPairSwapFailed`); the collect page does not.

On Hedera, a transfer can fail without any change on the Lynx side. A token's issuer can freeze an account (the strategy's or the pool's), pause the token, or revoke KYC. Of the current catalog's pair tokens, only USDC (`0.0.456858`) has a freeze key, and none has a pause or KYC key.

When a page fails, the router does the following:

1. It treats the failure as a phase-0 failure and runs phase 0 again, up to `MAX_PHASE0_FAILURES` = 8 failed attempts in total ([`_shouldStayOnPhase0()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxKeeperRouter.sol#L612-L636)). Each attempt is a paid scheduled execution.
2. It emits `LpHarvestGiveUp` and leaves phase 0.
3. [`_advanceOpsPhase()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxKeeperRouter.sol#L638-L650) aborts the pass, which resets the cursor to 0 ([`_completeHarvestPass()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/SaucerSwapLiquidityStrategy.sol#L852-L856)).

The next week's pass starts again from the first serial and fails at the same one. As long as the condition lasts, the serials after it are never collected.

#### Impact

Low. While a pair token cannot be transferred to the strategy:

- the fees of every later position are not collected, so they do not reach NAV;
- each week, eight scheduled executions are spent on a failure that is certain to repeat.

The fees are not lost, because they stay in the NFTs. The affected position cannot be decreased, closed or rotated until the token can be transferred again; that part is unavoidable. The trigger requires an action by the token issuer, and in the current catalog only USDC's issuer can take it.

#### Recommendation

Isolate collects per serial. Call the NPM's `collect()` in a `try`/`catch`, emit an event with the serial and the revert data on failure, and advance the cursor past the failing serial. Credit fees only for successful collects. Keep the close and rotate paths fail-closed for the affected position.

#### Developer Response

Fixed in commits [134250d](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/134250d866107287a19279836f1fb4fc49d9e433), [2354f6d](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/2354f6d2fcc571de0c7ac87db0feff471a1d6d06).

issues.title: A replacement mint deploys credited pair-token fees and erases their credit, so the fees skip the profit lock
issues.body:
#### Technical Details

`harvestFeeCredit[pairToken]` marks pair-token fees that the harvest has collected but not yet converted. [`_tryIdlePairTokenWhbarValue()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/SaucerSwapLiquidityStrategy.sol#L782-L806) excludes them from `impairmentValue()`. They reach NAV only after the swap page converts them and the WHBAR is reported as locked profit. When a harvest swap fails, the `catch` branch keeps both the tokens and their credit ([L929-L934](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/SaucerSwapLiquidityStrategy.sol#L929-L934)).

A rotate or widen before the next successful conversion breaks this:

1. [`_mintReplacement()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxLpAllocator.sol#L1354-L1380) deploys the strategy's full WHBAR and pair-token balances, including the credited fees.
2. `createLPPosition()` clamps the credit to the remaining idle balance ([L583-L584](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/SaucerSwapLiquidityStrategy.sol#L583-L584)), so the credit drops to zero or dust.
3. The fees now sit inside the new NFT, and `impairmentValue()` counts them immediately.

#### Impact

Informational. This matters only while the LP strategy is impaired. In that case, the next impairment sync reduces the impairment by the fee amount, and NAV rises at once instead of over the 7-day unlock. A depositor who entered before the sync captures part of the increase. Three conditions are needed: a failed harvest swap, a rotate or widen before a successful retry, and an impaired strategy. The amount is bounded by the stuck credit.

This is the same class as internal findings [#13](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/docs/audits/lp-range-manager-deep-audit-2026-09.md) (pair fees entering NAV unstreamed) and [#15](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/docs/audits/lp-range-manager-deep-audit-2026-09.md) (the rotate sweeps all balances). Today #22 makes both paths revert.

#### Recommendation

Leave credited pair tokens out of the replacement mint: subtract `harvestFeeCredit[pairToken]` from the pair balance in `_mintReplacement()`, so the next swap page converts them. Alternatively, report the credit as profit when it is deployed instead of clamping it away.

#### Developer Response

Fixed in commit [d234a53](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/d234a53e01b0b4183a80b23373bf342da5ff9cd3).

issues.title: `_clearPendingSchedule()` ignores the response code of `deleteSchedule()`
issues.body:
#### Technical Details

[`_clearPendingSchedule()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxKeeperRouter.sol#L794-L799) calls `HssOps.deleteSchedule(prev)` and discards the returned response code. It then clears `pendingSchedule` regardless of the result. Two functions use it: `stopWeeklyLoop()`, and `_scheduleNext()` before it creates the next schedule.

If HSS rejects the delete while the schedule is still pending, the router reports the loop as stopped, but the schedule stays armed:

- **After `stopWeeklyLoop()`:** the schedule later calls `weeklyOps()`. The call passes `onlyOpsExecutor`, because the scheduled call executes as the router itself. One phase body runs. The schedule does not reschedule itself, because `loopActive` is false.
- **In `_scheduleNext()`, with a schedule still pending** (for example, when the owner calls `weeklyOps()` manually): two schedules are live while the router tracks one.

On mainnet, the router's schedules use the router itself (`ContractID 0.0.10826535`) as admin key, so [hiero issue #22862](https://github.com/hiero-ledger/hiero-consensus-node/issues/22862), which concerns `DELEGABLE_CONTRACT_ID` keys, does not apply. On the normal path the delete returns `SUCCESS`; for example, schedule `0.0.10907633` at `1791299196.064620525`. The four `stopWeeklyLoop()` calls on mainnet returned `INVALID_SCHEDULE_ID`, but each one targeted a schedule that had already executed. For example, schedule `0.0.10850584` executed at `1788878000` and the stop came at `1788878869`. Nothing stayed armed. A rejected delete on a still-pending schedule requires a race with the schedule's own execution.

#### Impact

Informational. The case is rare, and the result is one extra phase execution.

#### Recommendation

Check the response code. Treat `SUCCESS`, and the codes meaning that the schedule no longer exists (already executed, already deleted, or `INVALID_SCHEDULE_ID`), as cleared. For any other code, emit an event and keep `pendingSchedule`. Do not revert on every non-`SUCCESS` code: the playbook's stop/start recovery after a 328 stops the loop on a schedule that has already executed, and that delete returns `INVALID_SCHEDULE_ID`.

#### Developer Response

Fixed in commits [c797493](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/c7974931f89e5436eafe2a38487bd9d495942d58), [2354f6d](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/2354f6d2fcc571de0c7ac87db0feff471a1d6d06), [426f684](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/426f684f654445299d637d5a6328ccd4a7577ab4), [3470f5f](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/3470f5fa3df95eaa393815494f06483ae98577b4).

issues.title: Range policies near the maximum width cannot be built when the TWAP is far from tick 0
issues.body:
#### Technical Details

[`setRangePolicy()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/LynxLpAllocator.sol#L400-L472) accepts `halfWidthTicks` up to `MAX_HALF_WIDTH_TICKS = 800_000` and `|centerOffsetTicks|` up to 100, without reference to the pool's price. At rotate time, [`planRotate()`](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/blob/0082743/hardhat/contracts/libraries/LpRangeMath.sol#L136-L163) centres the range on the TWAP. It reverts with `InvalidRange` when an edge falls outside `[MIN_TICK, MAX_TICK]`.

A policy with half-width `W` therefore cannot be built when `|TWAP tick|` exceeds about `887,272 − W − |offset|`. At the maximum width, this means about ±87,000 ticks. Each attempt reverts and consumes the week's rotate attempt (see #1).

#### Impact

Informational. Nothing is affected at current prices. On 2026-10-12, the catalog pools sat at ticks 69,930 (USDC), 43,737, 3,604, 25,866 and −20,424. For USDC, the pool with the smallest margin, a policy at the maximum width would fail only after a price move of about 5.5×. The issue needs both a near-maximum width, which is practically full range, and a pool far from tick 0.

#### Recommendation

When an edge crosses the tick bound, shift the range inward, keeping the width and keeping the TWAP inside the range. Otherwise, skip the target with a typed reason and do not consume the week's rotate attempt.

#### Developer Response

Fixed in commit [65e0bab](https://github.com/Lynxify-xyz/lynx-contracts/commit/65e0bab8c352448dd5355926eda9e6e123c920d3).
